premises.statement: Model only this finite same-direction paved patch for two seconds. Adopt no previously unobserved pedestrian, cycle, vehicle or debris entering it; no entry from distant rear traffic; distant forward vehicles continue away without reversing into it; opposing vehicles remain across the raised median. Retain the observed lead hatchback wherever its predicted body travels, including beyond this patch. This excludes unexpected crossings, median incursions, hidden obstacles and world-wide coverage. No road-containment feasibility is assumed.

Condition on the visible lead hatchback having approximately 4.5 m body length and 1.8 m width. Its reference rear silhouette is roughly 105–110 pixels wide, implying about 21–22 m camera-to-rear-face depth and approximately 24 m body-center range. These are falsifiable model size and perspective estimates, not measured dimensions or calibrated depth.

Assume locally approximately planar continuous pavement and no abrupt boundary change over two seconds. Estimate the left curb and right raised-median edge from reference perspective using the hatchback scale prior and supplied camera axes. Three visible same-direction lanes support approximately 10–11 m total paved width, not a widened single-lane corridor. The rear image supports continuation behind the current footprint; compensate its 0.025 s age using supplied ego history and assume stationary boundaries. Nonzero 0.5 m road residual represents approximate boundary, plane and scale error.

Reference appearance and approximately stable following range in the front sequence support forward motion, not parking. Adopt initial absolute longitudinal speed 9–13 m/s. Continue mode maintains this range; adverse braking mode permits acceleration -6 to 0 m/s² with speed floored at zero. Neither mode reverses. Continue lateral center displacement is bounded by 0.3t m; braking displacement by 0.5t m. Body yaw stays within 0.05 rad. The two modes exhaust only these adopted conditions. Rectangular sources include body rotation and all intermediate positions, before residual inflation.
